title: [finding][drivers] driver-memory's filter switch carries a `not in` arm for a spelling the spec's AST vocabulary does not define
body:
Observation only — no user-visible defect measured, nothing blocked. Recorded while working #9228 (PR #9235), which needed the exact membership-spelling set and therefore had to establish this.

## What was measured

`packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts:820` folds four spellings onto `$nin`:

```ts
case 'nin': case 'not_in': case 'notin': case 'not in':
```

`not in` (space-spelled) is **not** in the spec's AST vocabulary. `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`) declares exactly `in`, `nin`, `not_in`, `notin` for the membership operators, and `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` is derived from its keys — so:

- `isFilterAST(['stage', 'not in', [...]])` is `false`, and `parseFilterAST` never lowers the spelling;
- `canonicalAstOperator('not in')` returns the input unchanged, because `astOperatorLowering` has no entry for it;
- `metadata-protocol` answers `unrecognised operator "not in"` — pinned in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.malformed-filter.test.ts:128`, and `protocol.ts:866` carries a comment naming the case explicitly.

So no door lowers a filter into this arm. It is reachable only through the driver-local `{ field, operator, value }` condition-object path (`memory-driver.ts:761`), where a caller would have to hand the driver an operator string the protocol refuses.

## Why it is worth a line

It is a driver accepting a spelling the shared contract rejects — the tolerant-consumer direction Prime Directive #12 rules against, in the mildest possible form (an extra `case` label). Two ways it can go wrong later: someone reads the switch as evidence that `not in` is part of the vocabulary (it is what the #9228 dispatch did, from this same arm), or someone adds `'not in'` to `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` to "make the driver's arm reachable", widening the authoring vocabulary for no measured demand.

`driver-memory` is under the #5499 investment freeze, so this is deliberately filed rather than fixed: deleting a `case` label from a frozen driver is a decision, not a rider on an unrelated card. `driver-sql`'s `'not in'` occurrences are unrelated — those are the SQL keyword, not an authoring spelling.

## Suggested disposition when someone picks it up

Either delete the arm (nothing lowers into it, and the three real spellings stay), or, if the condition-object path really does receive it from somewhere, that producer is the thing to find and fix. Whichever way, the answer should come from measuring `memory-driver.ts:761`'s callers, not from the switch.
